messages.content: write a talk at a library. i want a short story but do not know which book to choose.

student: hello. could you help me find a book, please? worker: what kind of book would you like? student: a short story about a family. worker: would you like one about children? student: yes, that would be good. worker: here is one about two children and their grandmother. student: is it easy to read? worker: you can try the first page and see. student: thank you. i will read a little before i choose.
did the worker say i must choose that book?
no. the worker said you could try the first page before choosing.
now give me only the first thing to say.
hello. could you help me find a book, please?
write a talk about choosing soup at a restaurant. the person asks about cheese because they do not like it.

woman: could you tell me about the soup, please? worker: it is tomato soup. woman: does it have cheese in it? worker: no, but we can put some on top. woman: i would like it with no cheese, please. worker: would you like bread with it? woman: yes, please. worker: and what would you like to drink? woman: just water, thank you.
did the woman ask for cheese on top?
no. she asked for soup with no cheese.
what did she choose to drink?
water.
help me ask a worker at the station how to get to the next town. do not make up the train time.
you could say: hello. i would like to go to the next town. could you tell me which train to take and when it leaves, please?
i want to ask about the ticket too.
hello. i would like to go to the next town. could you tell me which train to take, when it leaves, and the price of a ticket, please?
can you tell me which train to take from this station?
i do not know which station you mean or when its train leaves. you can ask the worker about the train for that place.
give just the question about the ticket.
what is the price of a ticket to the next town, please?
write a simple talk about asking for a quiet room at a hotel.

woman: hello. do you have a quiet room? worker: would you like one away from the street? woman: yes, please. i would also like a window if there is one. worker: we have a room at the back with a window. woman: could i see it before i choose? worker: yes. please come this way. woman: thank you.
did she say she will take the room for sure?
no. she asked to see it before choosing.
make her first question shorter.
do you have a quiet room?
write a talk where a person asks if they should take their shoes off when visiting a house.

friend: hello. should i take my shoes off here? woman: yes, please. you can leave them by the door. friend: okay. where can i put my bag? woman: on the chair in the living room. friend: thank you. woman: come in and sit down. would you like tea? friend: water would be nice, thank you.
where do the shoes go?
by the door.
and the bag?
on the chair in the living room.
do they both go on the chair?
no. only the bag goes on the chair.
write a talk at a shop about a coat that is too big.

man: i like this coat, but it is too big for me. worker: would you like to try a small one? man: yes, please. do you have the same color? worker: yes. here is a small blue coat. man: thank you. this one feels right. worker: would you like to take it? man: i will think about it for a little while first.
did he choose to buy it in the talk?
no. he said he would think about it first.
what was still the same when the size changed?
the color was still blue.
write a talk where a child asks a teacher to look at one hard sentence.

student: could you look at this sentence, please? teacher: yes. which part is hard for you? student: i do not know if i should write is or are. teacher: who is the sentence about? student: two children. teacher: then use are. student: so i can write the children are reading? teacher: yes. that works. student: thank you. i can finish the rest now.
why did the teacher say are?
the sentence was about two children, not one child.
what if the sentence is about just one child?
then write: the child is reading.
write a talk where a man calls his sister while she is getting ready for work.

brother: hello. is this a good time to talk? sister: i am getting ready for work. can we talk later? brother: yes. when would be good for you? sister: after i get home this evening. brother: okay. i will try then. sister: thank you. i would like to hear about your day when i have time. brother: we can talk this evening. have a good day at work.
did she say she would never talk to him?
no. she asked to talk later when she has time.
make that shorter.
she asked to talk later, after work.
write a simple talk where someone asks to sit at a table in a library.

student: is it okay if i sit here? woman: yes. there is room on this side. student: thank you. should i move this book? woman: no, please leave it there. i am still reading it. student: okay. i can put my book here instead. woman: that is fine. student: i will keep my bag under my chair so it is not in the way.
did the woman give away her book?
no. she said she was still reading it and asked the student to leave it there.
where did the student plan to put the bag?
under the chair.
write a talk where a daughter asks if she can help her mother make dinner.

daughter: can i help with dinner? mother: yes, please. could you wash the tomato? daughter: should i cut it too? mother: i can do that part. you can put a plate on the table. daughter: okay. how many cups do we need? mother: three, one for each of us. daughter: i will get them. mother: thank you. we will be ready to eat after i finish cooking.
who was going to cut the tomato?
the mother.
what was the daughter asked to wash?
the tomato.
write a talk between two friends about coffee. one does not want milk.

friend: i am making coffee. would you like some? woman: yes, please, but no milk for me. friend: would you like sugar? woman: no, thank you. i like it as it is. friend: i like milk in my coffee. woman: that is fine. we can each have it the way we like. friend: here you are. woman: thank you.
does the woman say milk in coffee is wrong?
no. she only says what she would like in her own coffee.
so the friend can still have milk?
yes. the woman only asked for no milk in her own cup.
write a talk where a person asks a friend to give a book back before a visit.

woman: could you bring my book back today, please? friend: i have not finished it. do you need it now? woman: yes. my aunt is coming tomorrow, and i said she could read it. friend: okay. i can bring it this afternoon. woman: thank you. you can read it again after she gives it back. friend: that would be nice.
why did the woman need the book today?
her aunt was coming tomorrow, and she had said the aunt could read it.
did the friend say they would not bring it?
no. the friend said they could bring it that afternoon.
write a talk where one person is cold and another would like to keep the window open.

woman: i feel cold. could we close the window a little? friend: i like the air, but we can close it for now. woman: thank you. maybe we can open it again after tea. friend: that works for me. woman: i can also get a blanket. friend: then we can see how you feel after that.
did they have to say one person was wrong?
no. one felt cold, and the other would like some air. they found a plan they could both use.
make that shorter.
one felt cold, and the other would like some air. they chose to close the window for now.
help me ask someone how to find the library in a new town.
hello. could you tell me how to get to the library, please?
i do not want to sound like i know which road to take.
that question does not say you know the road. you could add: i am new here.
give me both together.
hello. i am new here. could you tell me how to get to the library, please?
should i ask them to say it again if i do not understand?
yes. you can say: could you say that again, please?
write a talk about two friends having tea after one finishes a hard piece of work.

woman: i finished the work today. friend: that is good to hear. would you like to have tea together? woman: yes. i do not want to do much, but tea would be nice. friend: we can sit by the window and take our time. woman: that is just what i would like. friend: i will get the cups. woman: thank you. i am happy it is done.
did they choose a big thing with many people?
no. they chose a quiet cup of tea together.
was it just the two of them?
yes. it was just tea with the two friends.
write a talk where someone comes to visit while a person is washing a cup.

friend: hello. is it okay to come in? woman: yes. i am just finishing this cup. friend: take your time. woman: please sit in the living room. i will come in when i am done. friend: can i help? woman: thank you, but it is just one cup. friend: okay. i will wait here. woman: i am done now. would you like some tea?
did she ask the friend to wash it for her?
no. she said it was just one cup and finished it on her own.
what did she do after finishing?
she asked if the friend would like tea.
write a talk where a person has to leave a call to get the door.

woman: there is someone at the door. i need to go now. brother: okay. would you like to call back later? woman: yes. i will call when i am free again. brother: that is fine. woman: thank you. i would like to hear the rest of your story when i come back. brother: i will keep that part for later.
make it shorter.
woman: someone is at the door. i have to go now. can i call back later? brother: yes. we can finish the talk then. woman: thank you. i will call when i am free.
did she say she was tired of the story?
no. she said she would like to hear the rest later.
write a talk where a boy asks his sister not to move his paper while he gets water.

boy: i am going to get some water. could you leave my paper here, please? girl: yes. are you still working on it? boy: i am. i just need a short break. girl: okay. i will use the other side of the table. boy: thank you. i will move it to my desk when i finish. girl: that is fine. there is enough room for both of us now.
did he say he would never move it?
no. he said he would move it to his desk when he finished.
why did he leave the table?
to get some water.
write a talk where a mother says there is bread instead of rice for lunch.

mother: we do not have rice ready today. would bread and cheese be okay for lunch? son: yes. could i have an apple too? mother: yes, there are apples in the basket. son: thank you. mother: would you like water or milk? son: water, please. mother: i will put it on the table. son: i can get the cups.
did the son ask his mother to make rice after she said there was bread?
no. he said bread and cheese were okay and asked for an apple too.
give his drink in one word.
water.
write a talk where friends would like to meet but do not know when they will be free.

friend: i would like to visit you. do you have a free afternoon? woman: i am not sure. can i tell you when i know? friend: yes. we do not have to choose right now. woman: thank you. i would like to see you too. friend: then we can find a day later.
make it shorter.
friend: i would like to visit. when would be good for you? woman: i am not sure. can i tell you later? friend: yes. we do not have to choose now. woman: thank you. i would like to see you too.
did they choose tomorrow?
no. they left the day open for now.
